title: Dynamically protected erasure qubit via low-frequency charge driving
authors: Ahmed Hajr, Ke Wang, Bingcheng Qing, Akel Hashim, Bibek Bhandari, Dominic Briseño-Colunga, Justin Dressel, Andrew N. Jordan, Irfan Siddiqi
abstract: Dynamical protection via strong driving can enable resilient quantum processing on imperfect physical hardware. However, the practical utility of such schemes is frequently limited by parasitic processes such as drive-induced dephasing and leakage. Here, we demonstrate that sub-GHz charge driving of superconducting Kerr oscillators (KOs) in the transmon regime circumvents this trade-off, simultaneously activating fast parametric interactions and protecting the encoded qubit from low-frequency noise. The key is the frequency dependence of the charge sensitivity: using the AC Stark shift as a probe, we find that the KO frequency sensitivity to a charge drive grows quadratically with both drive frequency and amplitude, making the oscillator weakly sensitive to $1/f$ charge noise yet strongly coupled to drives near 1~GHz. Exploiting this, we first demonstrate cooling and reset of the KO in 82~ns, to a residual population below $0.7\%$---lower than its $2.5\%$ steady-state thermal population. Next, using two KOs, we demonstrate logical control and dynamical protection of a dual-rail qubit with nearly fourfold erasure bias. Finally, using a single end-of-circuit erasure check, we achieve an error per Clifford of $5.6\times10^{-4}$, which falls to $1.5\times10^{-4}$ after post-selection, with 25~ns gates.
summary: This paper demonstrates a method to create noise-resilient qubits using superconducting Kerr oscillators driven by low-frequency charge signals. By exploiting the frequency dependence of the charge sensitivity, the system suppresses detrimental low-frequency noise while enabling fast quantum gates. This results in high-fidelity quantum operations suitable for quantum computation.
main_problem: Developing noise-resilient quantum processing schemes for superconducting qubits while minimizing hardware overhead, especially against low-frequency 1/f noise.
main_result: The authors demonstrated dynamical protection for a dual-rail qubit, achieving low error rates ($1.5	imes10^{-4}$ after post-selection) using sub-GHz charge driving on Kerr oscillators.
method: They exploit the quadratic frequency dependence of the charge sensitivity (AC Stark shift) to suppress low-frequency noise while maintaining strong coupling to microwave drives.
model_or_system: The system uses superconducting Kerr oscillators (KOs) in the transmon regime, implemented in a planar circuit, and employs a dual-rail encoding scheme for logical control.
key_observables: KO population (reset/cooling), logical error per Clifford, Rabi oscillations, and the AC Stark shift measurement.
important_parameters: Sub-GHz charge drive frequency, coupling strength ($g/2\pi \sim 50–200 	ext{ MHz}$), and detuning ($\Delta/2\pi \sim 0.5–2 	ext{ GHz}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the quadratic scaling of the Stark shift, which suppresses low-frequency noise, and the use of single-photon loss as the dominant error channel for the dual-rail code.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental schematic, AC Stark shift measurements, pulse sequences for parametric reset/cooling, and Rabi oscillations for qubit control.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from demonstrating basic cooling/reset of a single KO using low-frequency driving, to implementing logical control and dynamical protection on a dual-rail qubit, and finally quantifying the resulting error rates.
why_interesting: The work provides an experimental blueprint for building fault-tolerant quantum hardware by engineering the coupling mechanism to actively suppress environmental noise sources like 1/f noise.
